content:
經過十多年未在 Mac 手提電腦系列採用觸控螢幕，Apple 終於最快將於 10 月推出旗下首部配備觸控螢幕的 MacBook。新機將與下一代 MacBook Pro 重新設計同步發布，暫定名稱可能為 MacBook Ultra。

Of course, rumors are just rumors — but almost every credible source agrees that the MacBook Pro will gain touch support later this year. Apple even dropped a few hints in macOS 27: Sidecar touch support, pull-to-refresh, and slightly larger menu bar items.

As a 13-inch MacBook Air user, that last point is especially annoying, because content that used to fit to the left of the notch now spills over.

You can chalk it all up to coincidence, but the reality is probably exactly what it looks like on the surface. Either way, here's what the first touchscreen MacBook will bring.

OLED, Dynamic Island

On the display front, the redesigned MacBook Pro will feature a Tandem OLED display. Similar to what's used in the iPad Pro, which is often hailed as one of the best mobile displays on the market. Tandem OLED consists of stacked OLED panels, delivering excellent color, extremely high contrast, and higher brightness.

There are also reports that the new machine will feature Dynamic Island, and it will be slightly smaller than the one on iPhone. However, the new machine will not support Face ID.

Software optimizations

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple will make some special optimizations for the first touchscreen MacBook Pro, going beyond what's already visible in the macOS 27 beta:

"For example, when users touch a button or control, a brand-new menu will pop up around the user's finger, offering options more relevant to touch interaction. The software will also display the most appropriate set of controls based on the user's previous interaction history. Additionally, if users tap on a menu bar item at the top of the screen, that set of controls will enlarge for easier selection with fingers."

M5 Pro and M5 Max chips

Although initial reports suggested that the redesigned MacBook Pro would debut M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, Apple has now decided to skip this batch of chips to speed up M7 development. This means the first batch of 2nm chips will not be used in this redesigned MacBook Pro, and the new machine will continue with the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

However, a base model version will not be available for now. There are rumors that Apple will release a base model version of the redesigned MacBook Pro with an M7 chip as early as next spring.

Slightly thinner body

Regarding the design of the new MacBook Pro, one of the rumors is that the new machine will be slightly thinner and lighter — though it's unclear how noticeable the effect will be. The previous generation MacBook Pro made the computer look and feel quite thick, so a slight improvement in this area would likely be welcomed — provided thermal performance isn't sacrificed.

Summary

Overall, the first touchscreen MacBook Pro looks to be an exciting upgrade. With Apple raising prices back in June due to the memory crisis, the new machine will be priced even higher — so expect the 14-inch model to start at least at $2,499, and the 16-inch model at $2,999.

Are you excited about a touchscreen MacBook? Will you buy one immediately when it launches, or will you wait for the more affordable base model 14-inch version? Let us know in the comments.
